Read-only health check over an organizational demarkus knowledge system, the counterpart of `/soul-doctor` (local soul): report findings and fixes, **never write**.

Same `mark_*` tools over the broker (`mark_worlds`, `mark_graph`, `mark_backlinks`, `mark_list`, `mark_lookup`, `mark_fetch`, `mark_versions`); three differences shape every step:

1. **Multi-world.** URLs are `mark://<world>/<path>`; enumerate with `mark_worlds`, audit per world.
2. **Ephemeral graph store** (per pod, reset on restart): `mark_backlinks` returns only what this session crawled, so `mark_graph` runs before any backlink or orphan reasoning, every run.
3. **Cross-world references are checkable**: `mark_worlds` plus complete per-world inventories resolve `mark://<other-world>/<path>`, so the bare `mark://` reference check applies here.

## Scope

From `$ARGUMENTS`:

- **blank**: every joined system, all worlds. `"$HOME/.demarkus/bin/demarkus-plugin" registry knowledge-list` prints one joined system per line: its MCP server slug, reached through the destination server's `mark_*` tools. Nothing joined: suggest `/knowledge-join <broker-url>`, stop. Non-zero exit or malformed output: surface it, stop; never report an empty registry.
- **a slug**: that system, all its worlds.
- **`mark://<world>/`**: `mark_worlds` through every joined system, collect `(system, world)` matches; every directory call must succeed before deciding uniqueness or absence, else surface the failure and stop with scope unresolved. Exactly one match: audit it only, never expand. Several systems expose the name: ask which. None: report unavailable scope, stop.

Blank or slug scope: `mark_worlds` per system enumerates readable worlds (note `writable`; a fix is actionable only on a writable world). Enumeration failed or malformed: surface, mark that system incomplete, suppress its full-coverage conclusions, continue with systems that enumerated. Anchor each world on `mark://<world>/index.md`. Key every graph, inventory and report by system slug and world; never merge same-named worlds from different systems.

Read auth caveat: `mark_lookup` is filtered to the token, `mark_worlds` lists readable worlds only; the audit covers your visibility, never the whole system. Say so.

Deadline: five minutes from the first broker call, checked before every MCP call; on expiry stop starting calls, keep completed results, list skipped work, mark affected worlds incomplete, suppress conclusions that need missing coverage; an in-flight call cannot be cancelled, disclose when relevant.

## Gather (per world)

1. **Crawl.** `mark_graph` on `mark://<world>/index.md`, `depth: 5`; this also primes the graph store for `mark_backlinks`. Nodes `[status] <url> "title" N links` (note non-`ok` status and `(no title)`); edges `<from> -> <to>` (`mark://` internal, possibly cross-world; `http(s)` external).
2. **Inventory.** Directory queue from `mark_list mark://<world>/` with `include_archived: true`; `next-cursor` as `cursor` until `complete: true`, keeping `include_archived: true`; enqueue every returned subdirectory until the queue is empty. Track visited directories and a per-directory seen-cursor set; every incomplete page must return a non-empty cursor, different from the request cursor and unseen. Bound: 1,000 list calls in total (initial and continuation) or 20,000 documents per world; a bound makes coverage incomplete only when a required call or document remains; a terminal complete page at the bound with an empty queue is exhaustive. Any failure, truncation, partial-result marker or unavailable subtree: inventory incomplete; keep returned entries, list missing scope and exact coverage, suppress definitive orphan, missing-hub, broken-link and dangling-reference conclusions that depend on omitted paths. Cross-world conclusions use only complete inventories and crawls of in-scope worlds in the same system.
3. **Crawl disconnected documents.** Every inventory document absent from the root crawl's successful nodes (`[error]` included): `mark_graph` with depth 1.
4. **Bound.** At most 100 supplemental `mark_graph` calls per command, retries included, within the deadline; at a limit, report skipped documents, affected worlds incomplete.
5. **Retry once** per failed source while budget remains. A final failure leaves that source's outbound edges unknown: that world's orphan analysis incomplete, cross-world orphan analysis incomplete for every in-scope world it could link into, broken-link analysis incomplete for its edges; `[not-found]` findings confirmed by other sources stand.

## Core checks (graph plus inventory; fetches only for the bounded broken-link confirmations)

- **Broken links**: an edge whose `mark://` target is missing. Target in Nodes as `[not-found]`: confirmed, report, no re-fetch. Absent from Nodes: same-world, check the world's inventory; cross-world, that world's complete inventory only when in scope; out of scope, unreadable or incomplete: unresolved, not broken. A complete `mark_list` is still read-filtered, so confirm a same-world suspect with one `mark_fetch`, broken only on explicit `not-found`; other failures unresolved. Target `[error]`: next check.
- **Unroutable references**: an `[error]` node on a `mark://` link means the broker could not route the host; absence from `mark_worlds` does not prove it external. Readable host: retry once, report a persistent dispatch failure. Otherwise unresolved (unreadable, cross-system or stale); never claim absence or externality without evidence.
- **Orphans**: an inventory document, not the root hub, never the target of a `mark://` edge after complete root and supplemental crawls; report crawl coverage. Fix: add an inbound catalog link. Cross-world inbound counts only from fully crawled in-scope worlds of the same system.
- **Stale index entries**: broken links from an `index.md`.
- **Missing hub**: a subtree with documents and no `index.md`.
- **Untitled**: `[ok]` nodes shown `(no title)` (no H1 or declared title); on a `not-found` or `error` node that is the finding above, not a second one.
- **ADR sequence**: per `adr/` directory, duplicate or gapped `NNNN` prefixes, only with a complete inventory; else inconclusive with exact coverage.

## Deep checks (single world, or on request)

1. **Run the audit.** `mark_doctor` with `url: mark://<world>/` (`deep: true` on request) through the system's own server; it reads every document once, in code, and reports: untagged, untyped, **policy compliance** (missing axes, fields and tag values outside an axis's `allow_tags` list, judged under the world's `/.well-known/demarkus/policy.md` merged over the floor world's (root by default), each with the strictness), **policy floor** (a world policy line below the floor; the floor still applies), **secrets and personal data** (rule and line, never the value; personal data published under `content-check-override` is listed with its reason, not a fix; a secret has no override), duplicate content, hub shape, oversized, document shape, style (each finding opens with its rule id), in-body frontmatter, **style guide stale** (the floor world's `/.well-known/demarkus/style.md` whose rule table differs from the gate's), dangling and unlinked ADR references, and with `deep` metadata lost across versions. Tool error: surface verbatim, that world's deep checks incomplete. Its Coverage section lists what it could not read; carry every line into the report.
2. **Cross-world references** (the audit sees one world): per fetched body in the crawl, bare `mark://<other-world>/<path>` outside `[text](...)` and fenced code, resolved through the system's `mark_worlds` then that world's complete in-scope inventory. Host in another system, unreadable, out of scope or inventory incomplete: unresolved, not dangling. **Dangling**: no document in any complete in-scope inventory; fix: restore or drop; a body that annotates the absence is **known**, not actionable.
3. **Repair candidates** from the audit's metadata-lost findings are candidates, not verdicts (a later publish may have dropped fields deliberately); untagged since `v1` is curation, not loss. Confirm with the user before restoring. Repair (separate write step): force-fetch (an outline destroys the document); version moved: re-run the audit; `mark_publish` that body with the current map plus the recovered fields (policy axes, fields and allowed values re-checked), `retention` only if asked, `expected_version` current, `on_conflict: "fail"`; error or conflict: report, stop, document unchanged.

## Report

Plain, one line per system first (`<system>: <W> worlds, <N> docs, <X> findings`), then per world a `###` header with document count, `writable: yes/no` and `[coverage: your read scope]`, then one `####` section per check, most actionable first, `(<n>)` count, and `[deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]` on every deep-check section; one bullet per finding: URL, evidence, one-line fix. Examples:

```text
## <system> hygiene report

### mark://<world>/  (<N> docs, writable: yes/no)   [coverage: your read scope]

#### Broken links (<n>)
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md → mark://<world>/<missing>.md  ([not-found] node, confirmed): fix the link or restore the target

#### Unresolved / unroutable references (<n>)
- mark://<world>/index.md → mark://unknown/index.md  ([error], non-member or unreadable host): unresolved; verify membership or read access before calling it stale or external

#### Policy compliance (<n>)        [deep check, mark_doctor]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: tag category:howto is outside the allowed values for category (guide|decision) (strictness block); re-publish with an allowed category: value

#### Secrets and personal data (<n>)        [deep check, mark_doctor]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: secret/pem-private-key at line 12; treat the secret as compromised: rotate or revoke it, then remove it and re-publish; earlier versions keep it until the operator purges them
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: pii/canadian-sin at line 4; remove it and re-publish, or for a false positive re-publish with metadata content-check-override set to the reason

#### Dangling & unlinked references (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/adr/0006-….md → "ADR 0005", dangling: no such doc in any complete in-scope inventory; restore or drop the reference
- mark://<world>/architecture.md → "ADR 0006", unlinked: target exists but no in-body link; link the prose mention

#### Metadata lost across versions (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: candidate: tagged at v3 (category:ops + 6 tags, importance 0.7), none at v7; repair = force-fetch v7, publish that body with v7's metadata map plus the v3 fields (policy axes and require_fields re-checked), `expected_version: 7`, `on_conflict: "fail"`
```

Every other check follows the same bullet shape with its fix; a fix that writes is a gated update on a writable world. End with a short prioritized "what I'd fix first". "All clean" only when every check ran to complete coverage and found nothing; incomplete coverage (deadline, crawl failure, inventory bound, deep-check cap) lists confirmed findings, then the gaps; "no findings in the covered scope" only at zero findings.

## Don't

- Write to any world; a requested fix is a separate, explicit step against a writable world.
- Fabricate: nothing readable from `mark_worlds`, a hub `not-found`, or an empty registry: say so, stop.
- Imply coverage you lack: disclose worlds, document counts and deep-check sample size.
- Confuse with `/soul-doctor`: this audits the shared, broker-fronted systems.
